Our country has always been broken, but for an increasingly larger share of the population over the decades.

Athletes, workers… have always been commodities… always been exploited… and the degree to how badly has always gone in cycles.

For decades, power has been funneled up and up… and it continues to concentrate into fewer and fewer hands until one day the system is flipped.

Optimization is the removal of humanity from work and life flows to increase profit for the top.

People love to reminisce about the 90s, but the same issues existed then… they just hadn’t affected this many people to this degree. Yes, the market was freer, unions and benefits stronger, sports and restaurants less optimized, buying power better.

There were more times to be human and less optimal. There was room for imperfect, non-maximized profit. More time for family and friends. Nervous systems were healthier. Food was healthier. There was more time to be creative, innovative. More time to explore hobbies, interests, strengths…. For a larger share of people, that is. Communities were stronger. Social spaces were abundant. 

We sold ourselves out, but got better reinforcement in return.

But wealth’s tendency to concentrate slowly squeezed this country out of all of that. 

The race for ever increasing profits is the race to make everything shittier for everyone but the person above you. 

We’re all taking the rung of the ladder from the person climbing below us, and handing it to the person above us… and watching them take the rung from us. We’re playing ourselves lol.

So over the decades… life has become shittier for more and more people. To the point where people making 130k a year are making TikTok’s reminiscing about the lifestyle of a 2005 RadioShack employee. 

Got all these reels about people wanting to become millionaires just to be able to go to the grocery store, buy food, cook, and live in a shed with friends and family.

Nostalgia is at an all time high because more and more people miss the times when they felt more human… more alive. More present.

None of this is new… it’s just newer to a larger share of people. I think people are finally beginning to collectively realize it.

Those that downplayed the plight of those struggling in the 90s might be some of the same people finally seeing the issues today.

And those defending it today, might be the same people fighting against it 2-5-10-20 years from now.

I visit my local McDonald’s every week to meet up with my elder couple friends. I help them decorate the McDonald’s with festive decor. They bring their friends and we get to talk about everything. Real community. 

The spirit and humanity is still in everyone, and we have to find ways to keep it alive and bring it out of each other every day.
